Baseline `go test ./internal/app/` green on this tree. Live end-to-end reproduction performed with a binary built from the frozen tree (`go build -o /tmp/opencode/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan`) against a throwaway fixture workspace; target repo and workspace untouched; scratch cleaned.\n\n## Findings\n\n### F1 — Substring-sniffed exit classification lets workspace-controlled names and provider error text corrupt the documented exit-code contract (both directions)\n\n- **Category:** correctness/security-misuse of untrusted input in a machine-facing contract.\n- **Severity:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed (forward direction reproduced live; inverse direction proven by code path).\n- **Claim:** The sprint flow/execute/review CLI arms classify errors by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), …)` — `\"runtime\"` at sprint_commands.go:269, :363, :534 and `\"failed tasks\"` at :360 — *before* falling back to the typed `mapSprintError` ladder (:1028-1047). Error text embeds attacker/operator-influenced identifiers: project/sprint directory names reach messages verbatim through `project.RefError`/`sprint.RefError` (`%q`-quoted refs plus unquoted candidate lists, project/discovery.go:19-27, sprint/domain.go:348-356), and provider failure text reaches them through raw `*agentwrap.SDKError` propagation (service.go:604-608 → run_control.go:342 → CLI ladder). Any workspace entry whose name contains \"runtime\" therefore flips validation failures to exit 6, and genuine provider failures whose text lacks \"runtime\" are demoted to exit 4.\n- **Observable bad outcome:** Automation consuming exit codes misroutes decisions: a missing/ambiguous ref is treated as a retryable provider outage (exit 6, doc meaning \"runtime/provider error\"), while provider auth/rate-limit/model-unavailability (\"opencode run: rate_limit: OpenCode provider is temporarily rate limited or overloaded\") is reported as workspace/filesystem error (exit 4, code `validation.workspace`). Both contradict docs/cli-reference.md exit table (\"5: validation/reference\", \"6: runtime/provider\"). On the stable-listed `sprint review --json`, the stdout envelope says `\"status\":\"ready\"` while the process exits 6.\n- **Trigger / preconditions:** Any `sprint <p> <s> flow|execute|review` failing ref resolution while any project/sprint name in the workspace contains the substring \"runtime\"; or any flow/review runtime-stage failure whose SDK category is one of `authentication`, `rate_limit`, `provider_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`, `timeout` (no \"runtime\" substring). Dry-run flow is affected too (acceptance is skipped but the ladder is not).\n- **Evidence (reproduction, frozen binary):**\n  - Workspace contains only `projects/runtime-metrics`:\n    - `ultraplan sprint benign-metrics 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → stderr `project reference \"benign-metrics\" not found; available: runtime-metrics` → **EXIT=6** (expected 5).\n    - `ultraplan sprint tools 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → same candidates text → **EXIT=6**.\n    - Same workspace, typed mapper path: `ultraplan sprint runtime-metrics 01-alpha status` (missing sprint) → **EXIT=5** — divergence between sibling verbs for equivalent inputs.\n    - Renaming the ref so the quoted ref itself carries the substring (`runtime-tools`) also yields 6.\n- **Execution/data path:** argv refs → `Service.Flow/Review` → `resolveSprintInputs*` → `ResolveProject/ResolveSprint` RefError text → CLI ladder `Contains(err.Error(),\"runtime\")` → `classified(ExitRuntime,…)`; inverse: agentwrap SDK error → `mapError` (redaction only, runtime/runtime.go:752-775) → unwrapped through controlledRuntime.StartRun (run_control.go:342) and FlowRequirements (service.go:608) → ladder no-match → `mapSprintError` default → ExitWorkspace(4).\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** Typed mappers exist and are used by `status`, `verify`, QA, smoke, study, and run doors — verify is clean, proving the correct pattern is available in-tree. Findings-bearing failures short-circuit to ExitValidation before the substring check, so the flip needs findings-free errors (refs, provider transport, persistence). Tests never drive these branches: the only app-level flow→ExitRuntime pin (sprint_commands_test.go:583-594) exercises a classed run-control persistence error returned before the ladder, and the fake runtime (sprint_commands_test.go:918-950) never fails; no test pins auth/rate-limit classification. No doc blesses string matching; agentwrap's own contract explicitly classifies \"without string matching\" (agentwrap errors.go:9), which this layer re-introduces.\n- **False-positive analysis:** Considered whether lower layers guarantee fixed prefixes containing \"runtime\" (many do say \"runtime is required…\"), but ref/candidate text and non-\"runtime\" categories demonstrably reach the ladders. Considered whether refs could be pre-validated at dispatch — they are not; args pass straight into services after config load.\n- **Required fix direction:** Delete the substring branches; classify via typed signals only (extend `mapSprintError` with the runtime/partial cases as typed sentinels or `errors.As` on `*runtimepkg.Error`/SDK categories). If message sniffing must survive transitionally, restrict it to structured fields (e.g., `Result.Runtime.Status`) never free text.\n- **Required regression test:** Table-driven app tests over `flow --dry-run` with (a) missing project in a workspace containing a `projects/runtime-x` entry asserting exit 5 + empty stdout, (b) stubbed runtime returning an `authentication`-category error asserting exit 6; plus a pin that `review --json` envelope status and process class agree on ref failure.\n\n### F2 — `study init` clone URLs are unvalidated (git option-injection primitive) and remote git output reaches the operator terminal without control-character sanitization\n\n- **Category:** security hardening / trust-boundary hygiene.\n- **Severity:** P3. **Confidence:** high on code facts; medium on exploitability (see honest limits below).\n- **Claim (a):** `source.url` from study-init.yml is validated only for presence (init_yaml.go:147-149); no scheme/format check precedes `exec.Command(\"git\", \"clone\", \"--depth\", \"1\", url, dest)` (init_clone.go:44-50). A URL beginning with `-` is parsed by git as client options — the standard git option-injection primitive (`--upload-pack=<cmd>` executes `<cmd>` locally when the repository argument exists; verified against git 2.55: `git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=\"touch …\" ./repo ./target` created the file).\n- **Honest limit:** Under today's call shape the repository argument is `dest` (`studies/<s>/sources/<name>`), which never exists when clones run, so git aborts (\"repository does not exist\") before any transport option fires. I verified end-to-end through the frozen binary that a crafted yml exits 8 with the clone failing and **no** command execution (`ext::` is blocked by default in modern git; upload-pack does not fire on the nonexistent repo). This is a dangerous primitive plus latent risk (any future change that reorders args, reuses an existing destination, or adds `-c` plumbing turns it into local RCE via a repo-supplied yml in a tool whose workflow is \"bootstrap studies from repos\").\n- **Claim (b):** On clone failure, `CombinedOutput` (remote-controlled sideband/\"remote:\" text included) flows through `redactGitOutput` (credential-URL regex + truncation only — init_clone.go:52-65) into `ClonePartialError.Failures[].Err` and is printed verbatim to stderr (study_commands.go:1477) and again via `fail()` (app.go:233). ANSI escapes/control bytes from a hostile git remote (or HTTP MITM) reach the operator terminal. The codebase's own `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278) strips exactly these bytes for JSON/TUI surfaces, demonstrating the intended control exists but is not applied on the human stderr path; cli-reference.md commits to sanitized output (\"message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed\").\n- **Trust boundary:** network git remote / cloned-repo-supplied YAML → operator terminal, bypassing the established sanitization seam.\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** No shell interpolation (exec form is safe); dest paths are safe-name constrained and containment-checked; credential URLs are redacted; clone runs only after explicit operator invocation of `study init` with a chosen file.\n- **Required fix direction:** Enforce an allowlist (`https://`/`http://` scheme or `owner/repo` shorthand; reject leading `-`) before cloning, and route redacted clone output through control-char stripping (reuse displaySafe semantics minus newline handling) wherever it reaches stderr.\n- **Required regression test:** unit test rejecting `--upload-pack=…`, `-c…`, `ext::…`, and relative-path URLs at plan validation; test asserting ESC bytes injected into a fake CloneRunner's output do not appear in stderr bytes.\n\n## Defended non-issues\n\n1. **`serve --listen` loopback validation** (serve_commands.go:119-139): numeric-only `net.ParseIP` + `IsLoopback`, zone rejection, port bounds, whitespace rejection; validated before workspace discovery (test-pinned order). DNS names, octal/hex literals, and unbracketed IPv6 all fail closed. Non-issue.\n2. **TTY-less confirmation prompts** (defaults_commands.go:125-144, skills_commands.go:148-167, study_commands.go:277-316): EOF/non-\"yes\" deterministically take the conservative branch (keep files / refuse replacement with ExitPartial); destructive automation requires explicit `--force`/`--yes`; reset confirmation precedes durable acceptance so refused resets create no runs. Piped-stdin accidents require stdin content that is literally yes/y. Non-issue under the documented flag-gated automation model.\n3. **`code --output` writes outside the workspace** (code_commands.go:56-66): explicit operator flag, absolute-or-cwd resolution — capability-equivalent to shell redirection on the same machine; contrast `study prompt --output` which is correctly contained via `workspace.ResolveInside`. Not a vulnerability under the stated trust boundary; noting the asymmetry only as intentional-looking design.\n4. **Secret disclosure via renderers:** `config show` renders only `config.Redact(effective)`; health/status/QA/study messages pass `config.RedactValue` at every sink I traced; `smoke.environment` cannot carry values (validated `[A-Z_0-9]` names only, config.go:501-505,577-587); env summary prints counts, not values. Found no secret-bearing sink on stdout/stderr outside F2(b)'s remote-output path.\n5. **`openBrowser` subprocess** (main.go:45-62): exec form (no shell), target derived from the strictly validated listen address, 5 s timeout. Non-issue.\n6. **Durable acceptance coverage:** all ten inventory-pinned runtime-backed call sites accept before runtime work; parse/discover/config failures occur before acceptance so malformed invocations create no rows (verified ordering per arm). Caveat for the spine review: `TestEveryRuntimeBackedCLIEntryUsesDurableAcceptanceInventory` pins call counts and kind strings textually but would not catch a brand-new file adding runtime-backed work with zero `beginDurableCLICommand` calls unless its case row is added.\n7. **QA cancellation→8 vs generic→7 asymmetry and dual envelope families:** both match their in-tree contracts (cli-reference.md:363 documents the QA mapping explicitly; phase3-json-schemas.md fixes schema_version additivity). Contract ambiguity for unnamed envelopes (flow/metrics/storage) is a documentation gap, not a defect with an observable bad outcome beyond consumer confusion already flagged by the context pack.\n\n## Verification notes\n\n- Forward-direction reproduction used only the frozen binary and a scratch workspace; commands and outputs quoted above were captured verbatim during this session.\n- Inverse-direction chain verified line-by-line (no wrapping introduces \"runtime\" between agentwrap and the ladder); realistic rate-limit rendering taken from the pinned agentwrap module source (v0.0.0-20260825130518-dccd575bd101).\n- Git injection primitives tested directly against git 2.55.0 and end-to-end through the binary; negative results reported as negative results.\nRESULT" action.permission=bash action.action=allow action.pattern=*

Live end-to-end reproduction performed with a binary built from the frozen tree (`go build -o /tmp/opencode/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan`) against a throwaway fixture workspace; target repo and workspace untouched; scratch cleaned.\n\n## Findings\n\n### F1 — Substring-sniffed exit classification lets workspace-controlled names and provider error text corrupt the documented exit-code contract (both directions)\n\n- **Category:** correctness/security-misuse of untrusted input in a machine-facing contract.\n- **Severity:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed (forward direction reproduced live; inverse direction proven by code path).\n- **Claim:** The sprint flow/execute/review CLI arms classify errors by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), …)` — `\"runtime\"` at sprint_commands.go:269, :363, :534 and `\"failed tasks\"` at :360 — *before* falling back to the typed `mapSprintError` ladder (:1028-1047). Error text embeds attacker/operator-influenced identifiers: project/sprint directory names reach messages verbatim through `project.RefError`/`sprint.RefError` (`%q`-quoted refs plus unquoted candidate lists, project/discovery.go:19-27, sprint/domain.go:348-356), and provider failure text reaches them through raw `*agentwrap.SDKError` propagation (service.go:604-608 → run_control.go:342 → CLI ladder). Any workspace entry whose name contains \"runtime\" therefore flips validation failures to exit 6, and genuine provider failures whose text lacks \"runtime\" are demoted to exit 4.\n- **Observable bad outcome:** Automation consuming exit codes misroutes decisions: a missing/ambiguous ref is treated as a retryable provider outage (exit 6, doc meaning \"runtime/provider error\"), while provider auth/rate-limit/model-unavailability (\"opencode run: rate_limit: OpenCode provider is temporarily rate limited or overloaded\") is reported as workspace/filesystem error (exit 4, code `validation.workspace`). On the stable-listed `sprint review --json`, the stdout envelope says `\"status\":\"ready\"` while the process exits 6.\n- **Trigger / preconditions:** Any `sprint <p> <s> flow|execute|review` failing ref resolution while any project/sprint name in the workspace contains the substring \"runtime\"; or any flow/review runtime-stage failure whose SDK category is one of `authentication`, `rate_limit`, `provider_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`, `timeout` (no \"runtime\" substring). Dry-run flow is affected too (acceptance is skipped but the ladder is not).\n- **Evidence (reproduction, frozen binary):**\n  - Workspace contains only `projects/runtime-metrics`:\n    - `ultraplan sprint benign-metrics 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → stderr `project reference \"benign-metrics\" not found; available: runtime-metrics` → **EXIT=6** (expected 5).\n    - `ultraplan sprint tools 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → same candidates text → **EXIT=6**.\n    - Same workspace, typed mapper path: `ultraplan sprint runtime-metrics 01-alpha status` (missing sprint) → **EXIT=5** — divergence between sibling verbs for equivalent inputs.\n    - Renaming the ref so the quoted ref itself carries the substring (`runtime-tools`) also yields 6.\n- **Execution/data path:** argv refs → `Service.Flow/Review` → `resolveSprintInputs*` → `ResolveProject/ResolveSprint` RefError text → CLI ladder `Contains(err.Error(),\"runtime\")` → `classified(ExitRuntime,…)`; inverse: agentwrap SDK error → `mapError` (redaction only, runtime/runtime.go:752-775) → unwrapped through controlledRuntime.StartRun (run_control.go:342) and FlowRequirements (service.go:608) → ladder no-match → `mapSprintError` default → ExitWorkspace(4).\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** Typed mappers exist and are used by `status`, `verify`, QA, smoke, study, and run doors — verify is clean, proving the correct pattern is available in-tree. Findings-bearing failures short-circuit to ExitValidation before the substring check, so the flip needs findings-free errors (refs, provider transport, persistence). Tests never drive these branches: the only app-level flow→ExitRuntime pin (sprint_commands_test.go:583-594) exercises a classed run-control persistence error returned before the ladder, and the fake runtime (sprint_commands_test.go:918-950) never fails; no test pins auth/rate-limit classification. No doc blesses string matching; agentwrap's own contract explicitly classifies \"without string matching\" (agentwrap errors.go:9), which this layer re-introduces.\n- **False-positive analysis:** Considered whether lower layers guarantee fixed prefixes containing \"runtime\" (many do say \"runtime is required…\"), but ref/candidate text and non-\"runtime\" categories demonstrably reach the ladders. Considered whether refs could be pre-validated at dispatch — they are not; args pass straight into services after config load.\n- **Required fix direction:** Delete the substring branches; classify via typed signals only (extend `mapSprintError` with the runtime/partial cases as typed sentinels or `errors.As` on `*runtimepkg.Error`/SDK categories). If message sniffing must survive transitionally, restrict it to structured fields (e.g., `Result.Runtime.Status`) never free text.\n- **Required regression test:** Table-driven app tests over `flow --dry-run` with (a) missing project in a workspace containing a `projects/runtime-x` entry asserting exit 5 + empty stdout, (b) stubbed runtime returning an `authentication`-category error asserting exit 6; plus a pin that `review --json` envelope status and process class agree on ref failure.\n\n### F2 — `study init` clone URLs are unvalidated (git option-injection primitive) and remote git output reaches the operator terminal without control-character sanitization\n\n- **Category:** security hardening / trust-boundary hygiene.\n- **Severity:** P3. **Confidence:** high on code facts; medium on exploitability (see honest limits below).\n- **Claim (a):** `source.url` from study-init.yml is validated only for presence (init_yaml.go:147-149); no scheme/format check precedes `exec.Command(\"git\", \"clone\", \"--depth\", \"1\", url, dest)` (init_clone.go:44-50). A URL beginning with `-` is parsed by git as client options — the standard git option-injection primitive (`--upload-pack=<cmd>` executes `<cmd>` locally when the repository argument exists; verified against git 2.55: `git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=\"touch …\" ./repo ./target` created the file).\n- **Honest limit:** Under today's call shape the repository argument is `dest` (`studies/<s>/sources/<name>`), which never exists when clones run, so git aborts (\"repository does not exist\") before any transport option fires. I verified end-to-end through the frozen binary that a crafted yml exits 8 with the clone failing and **no** command execution (`ext::` is blocked by default in modern git; upload-pack does not fire on the nonexistent repo). This is a dangerous primitive plus latent risk (any future change that reorders args, reuses an existing destination, or adds `-c` plumbing turns it into local RCE via a repo-supplied yml in a tool whose workflow is \"bootstrap studies from repos\").\n- **Claim (b):** On clone failure, `CombinedOutput` (remote-controlled sideband/\"remote:\" text included) flows through `redactGitOutput` (credential-URL regex + truncation only — init_clone.go:52-65) into `ClonePartialError.Failures[].Err` and is printed verbatim to stderr (study_commands.go:1477) and again via `fail()` (app.go:233). ANSI escapes/control bytes from a hostile git remote (or HTTP MITM) reach the operator terminal. The codebase's own `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278) strips exactly these bytes for JSON/TUI surfaces, demonstrating the intended control exists but is not applied on the human stderr path; cli-reference.md commits to sanitized output (\"message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed\").\n- **Trust boundary:** network git remote / cloned-repo-supplied YAML → operator terminal, bypassing the established sanitization seam.\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** No shell interpolation (exec form is safe); dest paths are safe-name constrained and containment-checked; credential URLs are redacted; clone runs only after explicit operator invocation of `study init` with a chosen file.\n- **Required fix direction:** Enforce an allowlist (`https://`/`http://` scheme or `owner/repo` shorthand; reject leading `-`) before cloning, and route redacted clone output through control-char stripping (reuse displaySafe semantics minus newline handling) wherever it reaches stderr.\n- **Required regression test:** unit test rejecting `--upload-pack=…`, `-c…`, `ext::…`, and relative-path URLs at plan validation; test asserting ESC bytes injected into a fake CloneRunner's output do not appear in stderr bytes.\n\n## Defended non-issues\n\n1. **`serve --listen` loopback validation** (serve_commands.go:119-139): numeric-only `net.ParseIP` + `IsLoopback`, zone rejection, port bounds, whitespace rejection; validated before workspace discovery (test-pinned order). DNS names, octal/hex literals, and unbracketed IPv6 all fail closed. Non-issue.\n2. **TTY-less confirmation prompts** (defaults_commands.go:125-144, skills_commands.go:148-167, study_commands.go:277-316): EOF/non-\"yes\" deterministically take the conservative branch (keep files / refuse replacement with ExitPartial); destructive automation requires explicit `--force`/`--yes`; reset confirmation precedes durable acceptance so refused resets create no runs. Non-issue under the documented flag-gated automation model.\n3. **`code --output` writes outside the workspace** (code_commands.go:56-66): explicit operator flag, absolute-or-cwd resolution — capability-equivalent to shell redirection on the same machine; contrast `study prompt --output` which is correctly contained via `workspace.ResolveInside`. Live end-to-end reproduction performed with a binary built from the frozen tree (`go build -o /tmp/opencode/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan`) against a throwaway fixture workspace; target repo and workspace untouched; scratch cleaned.\n\n## Findings\n\n### F1 — Substring-sniffed exit classification lets workspace-controlled names and provider error text corrupt the documented exit-code contract (both directions)\n\n- **Category:** correctness/security-misuse of untrusted input in a machine-facing contract.\n- **Severity:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed (forward direction reproduced live; inverse direction proven by code path).\n- **Claim:** The sprint flow/execute/review CLI arms classify errors by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), …)` — `\"runtime\"` at sprint_commands.go:269, :363, :534 and `\"failed tasks\"` at :360 — *before* falling back to the typed `mapSprintError` ladder (:1028-1047). Error text embeds attacker/operator-influenced identifiers: project/sprint directory names reach messages verbatim through `project.RefError`/`sprint.RefError` (`%q`-quoted refs plus unquoted candidate lists, project/discovery.go:19-27, sprint/domain.go:348-356), and provider failure text reaches them through raw `*agentwrap.SDKError` propagation (service.go:604-608 → run_control.go:342 → CLI ladder). Any workspace entry whose name contains \"runtime\" therefore flips validation failures to exit 6, and genuine provider failures whose text lacks \"runtime\" are demoted to exit 4.\n- **Observable bad outcome:** Automation consuming exit codes misroutes decisions: a missing/ambiguous ref is treated as a retryable provider outage (exit 6, doc meaning \"runtime/provider error\"), while provider auth/rate-limit/model-unavailability (\"opencode run: rate_limit: OpenCode provider is temporarily rate limited or overloaded\") is reported as workspace/filesystem error (exit 4, code `validation.workspace`). Both contradict docs/cli-reference.md exit table (\"5: validation/reference\", \"6: runtime/provider\"). On the stable-listed `sprint review --json`, the stdout envelope says `\"status\":\"ready\"` while the process exits 6.\n- **Trigger / preconditions:** Any `sprint <p> <s> flow|execute|review` failing ref resolution while any project/sprint name in the workspace contains the substring \"runtime\"; or any flow/review runtime-stage failure whose SDK category is one of `authentication`, `rate_limit`, `provider_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`, `timeout` (no \"runtime\" substring). Dry-run flow is affected too (acceptance is skipped but the ladder is not).\n- **Evidence (reproduction, frozen binary):**\n  - Workspace contains only `projects/runtime-metrics`:\n    - `ultraplan sprint benign-metrics 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → stderr `project reference \"benign-metrics\" not found; available: runtime-metrics` → **EXIT=6** (expected 5).\n    - `ultraplan sprint tools 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → same candidates text → **EXIT=6**.\n    - Same workspace, typed mapper path: `ultraplan sprint runtime-metrics 01-alpha status` (missing sprint) → **EXIT=5** — divergence between sibling verbs for equivalent inputs.\n    - Renaming the ref so the quoted ref itself carries the substring (`runtime-tools`) also yields 6.\n- **Execution/data path:** argv refs → `Service.Flow/Review` → `resolveSprintInputs*` → `ResolveProject/ResolveSprint` RefError text → CLI ladder `Contains(err.Error(),\"runtime\")` → `classified(ExitRuntime,…)`; inverse: agentwrap SDK error → `mapError` (redaction only, runtime/runtime.go:752-775) → unwrapped through controlledRuntime.StartRun (run_control.go:342) and FlowRequirements (service.go:608) → ladder no-match → `mapSprintError` default → ExitWorkspace(4).\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** Typed mappers exist and are used by `status`, `verify`, QA, smoke, study, and run doors — verify is clean, proving the correct pattern is available in-tree. Findings-bearing failures short-circuit to ExitValidation before the substring check, so the flip needs findings-free errors (refs, provider transport, persistence). Tests never drive these branches: the only app-level flow→ExitRuntime pin (sprint_commands_test.go:583-594) exercises a classed run-control persistence error returned before the ladder, and the fake runtime (sprint_commands_test.go:918-950) never fails; no test pins auth/rate-limit classification. No doc blesses string matching; agentwrap's own contract explicitly classifies \"without string matching\" (agentwrap errors.go:9), which this layer re-introduces.\n- **False-positive analysis:** Considered whether lower layers guarantee fixed prefixes containing \"runtime\" (many do say \"runtime is required…\"), but ref/candidate text and non-\"runtime\" categories demonstrably reach the ladders. A URL beginning with `-` is parsed by git as client options — the standard git option-injection primitive (`--upload-pack=<cmd>` executes `<cmd>` locally when the repository argument exists; verified against git 2.55: `git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=\"touch …\" ./repo ./target` created the file).\n- **Honest limit:** Under today's call shape the repository argument is `dest` (`studies/<s>/sources/<name>`), which never exists when clones run, so git aborts (\"repository does not exist\") before any transport option fires. I verified end-to-end through the frozen binary that a crafted yml exits 8 with the clone failing and **no** command execution (`ext::` is blocked by default in modern git; upload-pack does not fire on the nonexistent repo). This is a dangerous primitive plus latent risk (any future change that reorders args, reuses an existing destination, or adds `-c` plumbing turns it into local RCE via a repo-supplied yml in a tool whose workflow is \"bootstrap studies from repos\").\n- **Claim (b):** On clone failure, `CombinedOutput` (remote-controlled sideband/\"remote:\" text included) flows through `redactGitOutput` (credential-URL regex + truncation only — init_clone.go:52-65) into `ClonePartialError.Failures[].Err` and is printed verbatim to stderr (study_commands.go:1477) and again via `fail()` (app.go:233). ANSI escapes/control bytes from a hostile git remote (or HTTP MITM) reach the operator terminal. The codebase's own `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278) strips exactly these bytes for JSON/TUI surfaces, demonstrating the intended control exists but is not applied on the human stderr path; cli-reference.md commits to sanitized output (\"message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed\").\n- **Trust boundary:** network git remote / cloned-repo-supplied YAML → operator terminal, bypassing the established sanitization seam.\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** No shell interpolation (exec form is safe); dest paths are safe-name constrained and containment-checked; credential URLs are redacted; clone runs only after explicit operator invocation of `study init` with a chosen file.\n- **Required fix direction:** Enforce an allowlist (`https://`/`http://` scheme or `owner/repo` shorthand; reject leading `-`) before cloning, and route redacted clone output through control-char stripping (reuse displaySafe semantics minus newline handling) wherever it reaches stderr.\n- **Required regression test:** unit test rejecting `--upload-pack=…`, `-c…`, `ext::…`, and relative-path URLs at plan validation; test asserting ESC bytes injected into a fake CloneRunner's output do not appear in stderr bytes.\n\n## Defended non-issues\n\n1. **`serve --listen` loopback validation** (serve_commands.go:119-139): numeric-only `net.ParseIP` + `IsLoopback`, zone rejection, port bounds, whitespace rejection; validated before workspace discovery (test-pinned order). DNS names, octal/hex literals, and unbracketed IPv6 all fail closed. Non-issue.\n2. **TTY-less confirmation prompts** (defaults_commands.go:125-144, skills_commands.go:148-167, study_commands.go:277-316): EOF/non-\"yes\" deterministically take the conservative branch (keep files / refuse replacement with ExitPartial); destructive automation requires explicit `--force`/`--yes`; reset confirmation precedes durable acceptance so refused resets create no runs. Piped-stdin accidents require stdin content that is literally yes/y. Non-issue under the documented flag-gated automation model.\n3. **`code --output` writes outside the workspace** (code_commands.go:56-66): explicit operator flag, absolute-or-cwd resolution — capability-equivalent to shell redirection on the same machine; contrast `study prompt --output` which is correctly contained via `workspace.ResolveInside`. Not a vulnerability under the stated trust boundary; noting the asymmetry only as intentional-looking design.\n4. **Secret disclosure via renderers:** `config show` renders only `config.Redact(effective)`; health/status/QA/study messages pass `config.RedactValue` at every sink I traced; `smoke.environment` cannot carry values (validated `[A-Z_0-9]` names only, config.go:501-505,577-587); env summary prints counts, not values. Found no secret-bearing sink on stdout/stderr outside F2(b)'s remote-output path.\n5. **`openBrowser` subprocess** (main.go:45-62): exec form (no shell), target derived from the strictly validated listen address, 5 s timeout. Non-issue.\n6. **Durable acceptance coverage:** all ten inventory-pinned runtime-backed call sites accept before runtime work; parse/discover/config failures occur before acceptance so malformed invocations create no rows (verified ordering per arm). Caveat for the spine review: `TestEveryRuntimeBackedCLIEntryUsesDurableAcceptanceInventory` pins call counts and kind strings textually but would not catch a brand-new file adding runtime-backed work with zero `beginDurableCLICommand` calls unless its case row is added.\n7. **QA cancellation→8 vs generic→7 asymmetry and dual envelope families:** both match their in-tree contracts (cli-reference.md:363 documents the QA mapping explicitly; phase3-json-schemas.md fixes schema_version additivity). Contract ambiguity for unnamed envelopes (flow/metrics/storage) is a documentation gap, not a defect with an observable bad outcome beyond consumer confusion already flagged by the context pack.\n\n## Verification notes\n\n- Forward-direction reproduction used only the frozen binary and a scratch workspace; commands and outputs quoted above were captured verbatim during this session.\n- Inverse-direction chain verified line-by-line (no wrapping introduces \"runtime\" between agentwrap and the ladder); realistic rate-limit rendering taken from the pinned agentwrap module source (v0.0.0-20260825130518-dccd575bd101).\n- Git injection primitives tested directly against git 2.55.0 and end-to-end through the binary; negative results reported as negative results.\nRESULT" action.permission=bash action.action=allow action.pattern=*

Baseline `go test ./internal/app/` green on this tree. Live end-to-end reproduction performed with a binary built from the frozen tree (`go build -o /tmp/opencode/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan`) against a throwaway fixture workspace; target repo and workspace untouched; scratch cleaned.\n\n## Findings\n\n### F1 — Substring-sniffed exit classification lets workspace-controlled names and provider error text corrupt the documented exit-code contract (both directions)\n\n- **Category:** correctness/security-misuse of untrusted input in a machine-facing contract.\n- **Severity:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed (forward direction reproduced live; inverse direction proven by code path).\n- **Claim:** The sprint flow/execute/review CLI arms classify errors by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), …)` — `\"runtime\"` at sprint_commands.go:269, :363, :534 and `\"failed tasks\"` at :360 — *before* falling back to the typed `mapSprintError` ladder (:1028-1047). Error text embeds attacker/operator-influenced identifiers: project/sprint directory names reach messages verbatim through `project.RefError`/`sprint.RefError` (`%q`-quoted refs plus unquoted candidate lists, project/discovery.go:19-27, sprint/domain.go:348-356), and provider failure text reaches them through raw `*agentwrap.SDKError` propagation (service.go:604-608 → run_control.go:342 → CLI ladder). Any workspace entry whose name contains \"runtime\" therefore flips validation failures to exit 6, and genuine provider failures whose text lacks \"runtime\" are demoted to exit 4.\n- **Observable bad outcome:** Automation consuming exit codes misroutes decisions: a missing/ambiguous ref is treated as a retryable provider outage (exit 6, doc meaning \"runtime/provider error\"), while provider auth/rate-limit/model-unavailability (\"opencode run: rate_limit: OpenCode provider is temporarily rate limited or overloaded\") is reported as workspace/filesystem error (exit 4, code `validation.workspace`). Both contradict docs/cli-reference.md exit table (\"5: validation/reference\", \"6: runtime/provider\"). On the stable-listed `sprint review --json`, the stdout envelope says `\"status\":\"ready\"` while the process exits 6.\n- **Trigger / preconditions:** Any `sprint <p> <s> flow|execute|review` failing ref resolution while any project/sprint name in the workspace contains the substring \"runtime\"; or any flow/review runtime-stage failure whose SDK category is one of `authentication`, `rate_limit`, `provider_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`, `timeout` (no \"runtime\" substring). Dry-run flow is affected too (acceptance is skipped but the ladder is not).\n- **Evidence (reproduction, frozen binary):**\n  - Workspace contains only `projects/runtime-metrics`:\n    - `ultraplan sprint benign-metrics 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → stderr `project reference \"benign-metrics\" not found; available: runtime-metrics` → **EXIT=6** (expected 5).\n    - `ultraplan sprint tools 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → same candidates text → **EXIT=6**.\n    - Same workspace, typed mapper path: `ultraplan sprint runtime-metrics 01-alpha status` (missing sprint) → **EXIT=5** — divergence between sibling verbs for equivalent inputs.\n    - Renaming the ref so the quoted ref itself carries the substring (`runtime-tools`) also yields 6.\n- **Execution/data path:** argv refs → `Service.Flow/Review` → `resolveSprintInputs*` → `ResolveProject/ResolveSprint` RefError text → CLI ladder `Contains(err.Error(),\"runtime\")` → `classified(ExitRuntime,…)`; inverse: agentwrap SDK error → `mapError` (redaction only, runtime/runtime.go:752-775) → unwrapped through controlledRuntime.StartRun (run_control.go:342) and FlowRequirements (service.go:608) → ladder no-match → `mapSprintError` default → ExitWorkspace(4).\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** Typed mappers exist and are used by `status`, `verify`, QA, smoke, study, and run doors — verify is clean, proving the correct pattern is available in-tree. Findings-bearing failures short-circuit to ExitValidation before the substring check, so the flip needs findings-free errors (refs, provider transport, persistence). Tests never drive these branches: the only app-level flow→ExitRuntime pin (sprint_commands_test.go:583-594) exercises a classed run-control persistence error returned before the ladder, and the fake runtime (sprint_commands_test.go:918-950) never fails; no test pins auth/rate-limit classification. No doc blesses string matching; agentwrap's own contract explicitly classifies \"without string matching\" (agentwrap errors.go:9), which this layer re-introduces.\n- **False-positive analysis:** Considered whether lower layers guarantee fixed prefixes containing \"runtime\" (many do say \"runtime is required…\"), but ref/candidate text and non-\"runtime\" categories demonstrably reach the ladders. Considered whether refs could be pre-validated at dispatch — they are not; args pass straight into services after config load.\n- **Required fix direction:** Delete the substring branches; classify via typed signals only (extend `mapSprintError` with the runtime/partial cases as typed sentinels or `errors.As` on `*runtimepkg.Error`/SDK categories). If message sniffing must survive transitionally, restrict it to structured fields (e.g., `Result.Runtime.Status`) never free text.\n- **Required regression test:** Table-driven app tests over `flow --dry-run` with (a) missing project in a workspace containing a `projects/runtime-x` entry asserting exit 5 + empty stdout, (b) stubbed runtime returning an `authentication`-category error asserting exit 6; plus a pin that `review --json` envelope status and process class agree on ref failure.\n\n### F2 — `study init` clone URLs are unvalidated (git option-injection primitive) and remote git output reaches the operator terminal without control-character sanitization\n\n- **Category:** security hardening / trust-boundary hygiene.\n- **Severity:** P3. **Confidence:** high on code facts; medium on exploitability (see honest limits below).\n- **Claim (a):** `source.url` from study-init.yml is validated only for presence (init_yaml.go:147-149); no scheme/format check precedes `exec.Command(\"git\", \"clone\", \"--depth\", \"1\", url, dest)` (init_clone.go:44-50). A URL beginning with `-` is parsed by git as client options — the standard git option-injection primitive (`--upload-pack=<cmd>` executes `<cmd>` locally when the repository argument exists; verified against git 2.55: `git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=\"touch …\" ./repo ./target` created the file).\n- **Honest limit:** Under today's call shape the repository argument is `dest` (`studies/<s>/sources/<name>`), which never exists when clones run, so git aborts (\"repository does not exist\") before any transport option fires. I verified end-to-end through the frozen binary that a crafted yml exits 8 with the clone failing and **no** command execution (`ext::` is blocked by default in modern git; upload-pack does not fire on the nonexistent repo). This is a dangerous primitive plus latent risk (any future change that reorders args, reuses an existing destination, or adds `-c` plumbing turns it into local RCE via a repo-supplied yml in a tool whose workflow is \"bootstrap studies from repos\").\n- **Claim (b):** On clone failure, `CombinedOutput` (remote-controlled sideband/\"remote:\" text included) flows through `redactGitOutput` (credential-URL regex + truncation only — init_clone.go:52-65) into `ClonePartialError.Failures[].Err` and is printed verbatim to stderr (study_commands.go:1477) and again via `fail()` (app.go:233). ANSI escapes/control bytes from a hostile git remote (or HTTP MITM) reach the operator terminal. The codebase's own `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278) strips exactly these bytes for JSON/TUI surfaces, demonstrating the intended control exists but is not applied on the human stderr path; cli-reference.md commits to sanitized output (\"message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed\").\n- **Trust boundary:** network git remote / cloned-repo-supplied YAML → operator terminal, bypassing the established sanitization seam.\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** No shell interpolation (exec form is safe); dest paths are safe-name constrained and containment-checked; credential URLs are redacted; clone runs only after explicit operator invocation of `study init` with a chosen file.\n- **Required fix direction:** Enforce an allowlist (`https://`/`http://` scheme or `owner/repo` shorthand; reject leading `-`) before cloning, and route redacted clone output through control-char stripping (reuse displaySafe semantics minus newline handling) wherever it reaches stderr.\n- **Required regression test:** unit test rejecting `--upload-pack=…`, `-c…`, `ext::…`, and relative-path URLs at plan validation; test asserting ESC bytes injected into a fake CloneRunner's output do not appear in stderr bytes.\n\n## Defended non-issues\n\n1. **`serve --listen` loopback validation** (serve_commands.go:119-139): numeric-only `net.ParseIP` + `IsLoopback`, zone rejection, port bounds, whitespace rejection; validated before workspace discovery (test-pinned order). DNS names, octal/hex literals, and unbracketed IPv6 all fail closed. Non-issue.\n2. **TTY-less confirmation prompts** (defaults_commands.go:125-144, skills_commands.go:148-167, study_commands.go:277-316): EOF/non-\"yes\" deterministically take the conservative branch (keep files / refuse replacement with ExitPartial); destructive automation requires explicit `--force`/`--yes`; reset confirmation precedes durable acceptance so refused resets create no runs. Piped-stdin accidents require stdin content that is literally yes/y. Non-issue under the documented flag-gated automation model.\n3. **`code --output` writes outside the workspace** (code_commands.go:56-66): explicit operator flag, absolute-or-cwd resolution — capability-equivalent to shell redirection on the same machine; contrast `study prompt --output` which is correctly contained via `workspace.ResolveInside`. Not a vulnerability under the stated trust boundary; noting the asymmetry only as intentional-looking design.\n4. **Secret disclosure via renderers:** `config show` renders only `config.Redact(effective)`; health/status/QA/study messages pass `config.RedactValue` at every sink I traced; `smoke.environment` cannot carry values (validated `[A-Z_0-9]` names only, config.go:501-505,577-587); env summary prints counts, not values. Found no secret-bearing sink on stdout/stderr outside F2(b)'s remote-output path.\n5. **`openBrowser` subprocess** (main.go:45-62): exec form (no shell), target derived from the strictly validated listen address, 5 s timeout. Non-issue.\n6. **Durable acceptance coverage:** all ten inventory-pinned runtime-backed call sites accept before runtime work; parse/discover/config failures occur before acceptance so malformed invocations create no rows (verified ordering per arm). Caveat for the spine review: `TestEveryRuntimeBackedCLIEntryUsesDurableAcceptanceInventory` pins call counts and kind strings textually but would not catch a brand-new file adding runtime-backed work with zero `beginDurableCLICommand` calls unless its case row is added.\n7. **QA cancellation→8 vs generic→7 asymmetry and dual envelope families:** both match their in-tree contracts (cli-reference.md:363 documents the QA mapping explicitly; phase3-json-schemas.md fixes schema_version additivity). Contract ambiguity for unnamed envelopes (flow/metrics/storage) is a documentation gap, not a defect with an observable bad outcome beyond consumer confusion already flagged by the context pack.\n\n## Verification notes\n\n- Forward-direction reproduction used only the frozen binary and a scratch workspace; commands and outputs quoted above were captured verbatim during this session.\n- Inverse-direction chain verified line-by-line (no wrapping introduces \"runtime\" between agentwrap and the ladder); realistic rate-limit rendering taken from the pinned agentwrap module source (v0.0.0-20260825130518-dccd575bd101).\n- Git injection primitives tested directly against git 2.55.0 and end-to-end through the binary; negative results reported as negative results.\nRESULT" action.permission=bash action.action=allow action.pattern=*

Now let me analyze what I've seen. Key observations so far:

**Observation A: `SaveFlowState` evidence backfill happens BEFORE the DB/file routing, using `LoadFlowState` — fine.**

**Observation B: Study `SaveRunState` DB branch**: when authoritative and `state.Complete`, it writes BOTH DB and file. But note the file write re-stamps `UpdatedAt = time.Now()` in `saveRunStateWithHooks` and RE-VALIDATES. Fine.

Wait, there's something subtle in study SaveRunState: when NOT authoritative (no row), file-only save. When row exists, DB save + optional checkpoint file. OK.

**Observation C: The BIG one — `LoadRunState` DB branch skips `compactRunStateDiagnostics`.** The pack mentions this. What does compactRunStateDiagnostics do? Probably trims large diagnostics blobs to bound memory/DB size. On the file branch, load compacts after validation. On DB branch, no compaction. Consequence: a state saved... wait, saveRunStateDatabase DOES compact before saving (line 45). So DB rows are already compacted at save time. Load not compacting means in-memory only; next save will compact again before persisting. So no persistent growth. Minor memory concern only. Not a defect.

**Observation D: Torn read in Store.Load (two autocommit statements).** Real. Header read at snapshot T1, items at T2 ≥ T1. Concurrent Save committing between yields old header + new items. Observable badness? Consider execute state: header contains Status fields? Let me check ExecuteRunState header fields — Project, Sprint, Target, PlanPath, PlanFingerprint, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt + Tasks separate. What else? Need to see the struct. Also FlowState header minus Stages: SchemaVersion, Project, Sprint, UpdatedAt, Review, Smoke, QA pointers. Review/Smoke/QA summaries live in HEADER. Stages are items.

Torn read scenario for flow: old header (Review=nil or older Review summary) + new items (stages further along). Load returns state where stages say review-stage complete but Review evidence block is from older save → gates might make wrong decisions. Validation would pass (structurally valid).

For execute: header has maybe Status? Let me check ExecuteRunState struct fully.

But hold on — is concurrent access actually possible? Multiple processes: CLI commands and web server can run simultaneously against same workspace (the design explicitly supports multi-process via WAL+busy_timeout). Within web server, single store shared across requests; concurrent requests could Save and Load simultaneously. So yes reachable.

However, how likely and how severe? It's a genuine consistency defect: readers can observe a record that never existed as a committed unit. The fix is trivial (wrap both queries in one read transaction). Report as finding with medium severity, high confidence in mechanism.

Let me also consider WAL snapshot semantics more carefully: In autocommit mode each statement runs in its own implicit transaction. modernc.org/sqlite honors that. So yes, two statements = two snapshots.

Actually wait — there's an even nastier variant of the torn read: between the header SELECT and items SELECT, a Save commits which DELETES stale items and adds new ones. Reader gets OLD header + NEW items. For flow: header.SchemaVersion old? Same version. Review/Smoke/QA old. Stages new. Then ValidateFlowState checks stage paths etc. — passes. Downstream consumers (review/smoke/qa gates) consult state.Review etc. — they'd act on stale verification evidence with newer stage statuses. Concrete but requires concurrency.

Alternatively simpler observable: study RunState header has counters? Let me check RunState struct. If it has e.g. CompletedAt / status fields derived from tasks, mismatch could fail validation → spurious operation failures. Let me check the structs.

**Observation E: dry-run mutates existing DB.** In `runStorage`, when dryRun=true, OpenSQLite/Ensure skipped. BUT the per-record probes (`RunStateInDatabase`, `FlowStateInDatabase`, `ExecuteStateInDatabase`) call `productstate.Existing(root)` which, if `.ultraplan/run-control.db` exists, calls `open(root)` → `createSchema` → `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS product_states/product_state_items/index`. 

Concrete bad outcome: workspace has run-control.db created by runcontrol (e.g., user ran any run-control command) but never imported product state. Admin runs `storage migrate --dry-run` to preview. Result: the two product tables + index now EXIST in the database even though "dry-run" promised no changes. Is that observable harm beyond principle? Yes, concretely:
1. The doc says preview. Help text says nothing about mutation. docs/migration-product-state.md says "Preview the migration" — implies non-mutating.
2. More importantly: schema creation on a DB that's under active use by runcontrol could contend, but that's weak.
3. Actually here's a sharper consequence: **dry-run flips subsequent behavior?** No—row presence flips authority, table existence doesn't. Tables without rows don't change loads. So the mutation is limited to DDL objects + WAL sidecar files. Still, a "dry-run" writing to the production DB violates its contract; and if the DB is read-only (mounted ro), dry-run FAILS with an error instead of reporting — hmm, actually that's an interesting operational case: read-only workspace + dry-run → Existing→open→createSchema fails (attempt to write a readonly database) → err returned → appendItem failed items?? Wait: RunStateInDatabase returns (false, err); migrate appends failed item per study/sprint! So dry-run against a read-only DB reports FAILED items instead of a clean preview, or worse: open fails ⇒ `Existing` returns `(nil,false,err)` ⇒ RunStateInDatabase returns error ⇒ item failed ⇒ exit 8. So a pure preview command errors out on read-only workspaces. That's a concrete failure path. Also on a CORRUPT db, dry-run reports failed instead of previewing from files.

Also note asymmetry: when DB absent entirely, dry-run works cleanly (stat not-exist → no probe). When present, probes mutate.

Severity: medium. Confidence: high — code path is plain. I should verify createSchema really executes DDL (yes, ExecContext). And verify Existing is reached during dry-run: yes lines 93, 147, 170 storage_commands.go call *InDatabase unconditionally of dryRun.

Test to prove: create workspace with studies/projects; create empty run-control.db via sqlite3 or via runcontrol.OpenSQLite; run `storage migrate --dry-run`; then inspect sqlite_master for product_states. Expect tables exist after dry-run ⇒ defect proven. Also test read-only scenario optionally.

**Observation F: authority-flip race between migrate import and concurrent save (lost update).** Sequence:
1. Live process P holds sprint S mid-execution, file-backed (no row).
2. P saves new state → SaveExecuteRunState → ExecuteStateInDatabase=false → writes FILE (newest state).
   Wait order: probe first, then file write. Interleave with migrate M:
   - M: ExecuteStateInDatabase → false.
   - M: LoadExecuteRunState reads file (state X).
   - P: probes false, writes file state Y (Y newer).
   - M: MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase(X) → row = X.
   Now: file=Y (newest), DB=X (older), DB wins all future loads. P's next save: probe true → saves Y' to DB. So loss window closes at next save IF one occurs. If P crashed/exited right after writing Y (e.g., execution finished, terminal checkpoint written to file only because probe said false... wait terminal write goes through same routing: probe false → file only. So final terminal state Y written ONLY to file. Row X (mid-flight) sits in DB and WINS forever. Resume/status/gates read X. The completed outcome recorded in file Y is invisible. That's permanent state divergence with concrete bad outcome: a sprint that completed shows as mid-flight; resume may re-run tasks; QA gates see stale evidence.

Trigger: running `storage migrate` while a sprint/study is actively transitioning. Documented? Unknown #11 says interaction unspecified; docs say nothing about requiring quiescence. This is a real defect class (check-then-act race across processes), though timing dependent. Severity medium-high, confidence high in mechanism (no locking spans probe→write; migrate has no coordination with live writers).

Can I prove with a test? Simulate: goroutine A loops saving states to file-backed record; concurrently run migration; detect final inconsistency (file newer than DB while row exists). Deterministic version: directly interleave the exact sequence using the exported functions with artificial pauses — but pauses need hooks. Could demonstrate by calling the internal functions in the right order within a test (white-box, same package sprint): 
1. Ensure no row.
2. stateX := load from file (older).
3. Manually write newer file state Y via saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks (bypassing routing).
4. Call MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase(root, sp, stateX).
5. Assert LoadExecuteRunState returns X while file has Y → proven divergence reachable purely by scheduling, no exotic timing needed (the window is between any writer's InDatabase probe and its write; migrate's own probe→import span is exactly this).

Actually even simpler and fully deterministic WITHOUT concurrency: the ordering inside a SINGLE SaveExecuteRunState call vs migrate isn't needed. The deterministic statement: "migrate imports the file content it read at time T; any later file change (by a writer that probed before the import committed) is silently shadowed." The white-box interleaving above proves reachability. Good enough as regression-test sketch.

Hmm wait — but step 3 in my sequence: writer P wrote file AFTER probing false. In a real single-threaded demo, I emulate P's decision using the same primitives. Fine.

**Observation G: schema_version stored but never validated on LOAD.** Validate* functions DO check state.SchemaVersion == expected after decode (ValidateRunState line 125, ValidateFlowState 298, ValidateExecuteRunState 188). And save stores state.SchemaVersion into the column AND header JSON retains schemaVersion field (header clone keeps SchemaVersion since only Tasks/Stages nil'd). So a row with wrong version → decoded header has wrong version → validator rejects on load. So version gate EXISTS post-decode via header JSON. Column itself unused, but header covers it. Not a defect. Good counter-evidence found — drop hypothesis G.

Wait — careful: does the header JSON include schema_version for study? cloneRunState(state) with Tasks=nil keeps SchemaVersion field. Yes. And validators check it. So downgrade/upgrade skew handled identically to files. Drop G. 

**Observation H: unknown-field tolerance asymmetry (plain Unmarshal on DB branch vs DisallowUnknownFields for flow file branch).** DB branch tolerates unknown fields. Since only these binaries write rows via validated saves, unknown fields could appear only from external tampering or forward-version writes... but forward-version writes are rejected at LOAD by schema version check (header carries version). Hmm: future version 3 header has extra fields + schemaVersion=3 → load decodes (tolerant), validator rejects version ≠2. Good. Current-version row with extra unknown fields can't be produced by current writers. External tampering = workspace-local attacker who could equally edit files (files are STRICTER though: DisallowUnknownFields catches typos/corruption in files; DB branch silently ignores corrupted-but-valid-JSON additions). Marginal. The realistic scenario: partial corruption/truncation of BLOB? Truncated JSON fails Unmarshal anyway. Unknown-field tolerance only matters for garbage that's still valid JSON. Low value; report as defended/non-issue or low-sev note? Doctrine says substantive findings only. I'll mention as non-issue with reasoning.

**Observation I: hash columns never verified on read** — decorative integrity; no contract claims detection. Non-issue per doctrine (dangerous primitive vs vulnerability). Skip or non-issue.

**Observation J: `Existing` swallows open error into enabled=false? No:** `loadRunStateDatabase`: `if err != nil || !enabled return ..., err` — propagates error. So corrupt DB → ALL study/sprint load/save operations hard-fail (LoadRunState line 28-29 returns err). And in migrate, failed items. Operational fragility but arguably correct loud behavior. However NOTE: `Existing` returns `(store, err==nil, err)` — when err != nil, store nil, enabled FALSE, err set. Callers propagate. OK loud. Not silent. Fine.

BUT what about `open()` failing inside `Existing` due to BUSY (createSchema times out after 5s)? Under heavy contention, every load/save errors out. Speculative; skip.

**Observation K: `Has` returns `err == nil, err`** — weird but correct.

**Observation L: Save's change-guard on header compares ONLY header_hash and schema_version.** Two different headers with identical sha256? Collision — ignore. But subtle bug: guard means if header unchanged, updated_at not bumped — intended. Items guarded individually. Sweep deletes removed keys. All good.

Edge: **Save with SAME header but DIFFERENT items updates items but leaves updated_at stale.** Cosmetic only.

**Observation M: Ordinals not rewritten when items unchanged but ANOTHER item deleted?** Sweep deletes; remaining ordinals keep old values; ORDER BY ordinal still preserves relative order. Gaps harmless. Fine.

**Observation N: duplicate item keys within one Save.** For flow: stage names unique (validated). Execute: task IDs unique (validated). Study: task IDs unique (validated). All three validators reject duplicates BEFORE save. So upsert-collides-duplicate case unreachable via adapters. Non-issue.

Between them another importer could insert → LoadRunState returns DB copy → migrate saves same content back. Benign idempotent-ish. Non-issue.

Baseline `go test ./internal/app/` green on this tree. Live end-to-end reproduction performed with a binary built from the frozen tree (`go build -o /tmp/opencode/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan`) against a throwaway fixture workspace; target repo and workspace untouched; scratch cleaned.\n\n## Findings\n\n### F1 — Substring-sniffed exit classification lets workspace-controlled names and provider error text corrupt the documented exit-code contract (both directions)\n\n- **Category:** correctness/security-misuse of untrusted input in a machine-facing contract.\n- **Severity:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed (forward direction reproduced live; inverse direction proven by code path).\n- **Claim:** The sprint flow/execute/review CLI arms classify errors by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), …)` — `\"runtime\"` at sprint_commands.go:269, :363, :534 and `\"failed tasks\"` at :360 — *before* falling back to the typed `mapSprintError` ladder (:1028-1047). Error text embeds attacker/operator-influenced identifiers: project/sprint directory names reach messages verbatim through `project.RefError`/`sprint.RefError` (`%q`-quoted refs plus unquoted candidate lists, project/discovery.go:19-27, sprint/domain.go:348-356), and provider failure text reaches them through raw `*agentwrap.SDKError` propagation (service.go:604-608 → run_control.go:342 → CLI ladder). Any workspace entry whose name contains \"runtime\" therefore flips validation failures to exit 6, and genuine provider failures whose text lacks \"runtime\" are demoted to exit 4.\n- **Observable bad outcome:** Automation consuming exit codes misroutes decisions: a missing/ambiguous ref is treated as a retryable provider outage (exit 6, doc meaning \"runtime/provider error\"), while provider auth/rate-limit/model-unavailability (\"opencode run: rate_limit: OpenCode provider is temporarily rate limited or overloaded\") is reported as workspace/filesystem error (exit 4, code `validation.workspace`). Both contradict docs/cli-reference.md exit table (\"5: validation/reference\", \"6: runtime/provider\"). On the stable-listed `sprint review --json`, the stdout envelope says `\"status\":\"ready\"` while the process exits 6.\n- **Trigger / preconditions:** Any `sprint <p> <s> flow|execute|review` failing ref resolution while any project/sprint name in the workspace contains the substring \"runtime\"; or any flow/review runtime-stage failure whose SDK category is one of `authentication`, `rate_limit`, `provider_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`, `timeout` (no \"runtime\" substring). Dry-run flow is affected too (acceptance is skipped but the ladder is not).\n- **Evidence (reproduction, frozen binary):**\n  - Workspace contains only `projects/runtime-metrics`:\n    - `ultraplan sprint benign-metrics 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → stderr `project reference \"benign-metrics\" not found; available: runtime-metrics` → **EXIT=6** (expected 5).\n    - `ultraplan sprint tools 01-alpha flow --to plan --dry-run` → same candidates text → **EXIT=6**.\n    - Same workspace, typed mapper path: `ultraplan sprint runtime-metrics 01-alpha status` (missing sprint) → **EXIT=5** — divergence between sibling verbs for equivalent inputs.\n    - Renaming the ref so the quoted ref itself carries the substring (`runtime-tools`) also yields 6.\n- **Execution/data path:** argv refs → `Service.Flow/Review` → `resolveSprintInputs*` → `ResolveProject/ResolveSprint` RefError text → CLI ladder `Contains(err.Error(),\"runtime\")` → `classified(ExitRuntime,…)`; inverse: agentwrap SDK error → `mapError` (redaction only, runtime/runtime.go:752-775) → unwrapped through controlledRuntime.StartRun (run_control.go:342) and FlowRequirements (service.go:608) → ladder no-match → `mapSprintError` default → ExitWorkspace(4).\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** Typed mappers exist and are used by `status`, `verify`, QA, smoke, study, and run doors — verify is clean, proving the correct pattern is available in-tree. Findings-bearing failures short-circuit to ExitValidation before the substring check, so the flip needs findings-free errors (refs, provider transport, persistence). Tests never drive these branches: the only app-level flow→ExitRuntime pin (sprint_commands_test.go:583-594) exercises a classed run-control persistence error returned before the ladder, and the fake runtime (sprint_commands_test.go:918-950) never fails; no test pins auth/rate-limit classification. No doc blesses string matching; agentwrap's own contract explicitly classifies \"without string matching\" (agentwrap errors.go:9), which this layer re-introduces.\n- **False-positive analysis:** Considered whether lower layers guarantee fixed prefixes containing \"runtime\" (many do say \"runtime is required…\"), but ref/candidate text and non-\"runtime\" categories demonstrably reach the ladders. Considered whether refs could be pre-validated at dispatch — they are not; args pass straight into services after config load.\n- **Required fix direction:** Delete the substring branches; classify via typed signals only (extend `mapSprintError` with the runtime/partial cases as typed sentinels or `errors.As` on `*runtimepkg.Error`/SDK categories). If message sniffing must survive transitionally, restrict it to structured fields (e.g., `Result.Runtime.Status`) never free text.\n- **Required regression test:** Table-driven app tests over `flow --dry-run` with (a) missing project in a workspace containing a `projects/runtime-x` entry asserting exit 5 + empty stdout, (b) stubbed runtime returning an `authentication`-category error asserting exit 6; plus a pin that `review --json` envelope status and process class agree on ref failure.\n\n### F2 — `study init` clone URLs are unvalidated (git option-injection primitive) and remote git output reaches the operator terminal without control-character sanitization\n\n- **Category:** security hardening / trust-boundary hygiene.\n- **Severity:** P3. **Confidence:** high on code facts; medium on exploitability (see honest limits below).\n- **Claim (a):** `source.url` from study-init.yml is validated only for presence (init_yaml.go:147-149); no scheme/format check precedes `exec.Command(\"git\", \"clone\", \"--depth\", \"1\", url, dest)` (init_clone.go:44-50). A URL beginning with `-` is parsed by git as client options — the standard git option-injection primitive (`--upload-pack=<cmd>` executes `<cmd>` locally when the repository argument exists; verified against git 2.55: `git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=\"touch …\" ./repo ./target` created the file).\n- **Honest limit:** Under today's call shape the repository argument is `dest` (`studies/<s>/sources/<name>`), which never exists when clones run, so git aborts (\"repository does not exist\") before any transport option fires. I verified end-to-end through the frozen binary that a crafted yml exits 8 with the clone failing and **no** command execution (`ext::` is blocked by default in modern git; upload-pack does not fire on the nonexistent repo). This is a dangerous primitive plus latent risk (any future change that reorders args, reuses an existing destination, or adds `-c` plumbing turns it into local RCE via a repo-supplied yml in a tool whose workflow is \"bootstrap studies from repos\").\n- **Claim (b):** On clone failure, `CombinedOutput` (remote-controlled sideband/\"remote:\" text included) flows through `redactGitOutput` (credential-URL regex + truncation only — init_clone.go:52-65) into `ClonePartialError.Failures[].Err` and is printed verbatim to stderr (study_commands.go:1477) and again via `fail()` (app.go:233). ANSI escapes/control bytes from a hostile git remote (or HTTP MITM) reach the operator terminal. The codebase's own `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278) strips exactly these bytes for JSON/TUI surfaces, demonstrating the intended control exists but is not applied on the human stderr path; cli-reference.md commits to sanitized output (\"message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed\").\n- **Trust boundary:** network git remote / cloned-repo-supplied YAML → operator terminal, bypassing the established sanitization seam.\n- **Existing controls / counter-evidence:** No shell interpolation (exec form is safe); dest paths are safe-name constrained and containment-checked; credential URLs are redacted; clone runs only after explicit operator invocation of `study init` with a chosen file.\n- **Required fix direction:** Enforce an allowlist (`https://`/`http://` scheme or `owner/repo` shorthand; reject leading `-`) before cloning, and route redacted clone output through control-char stripping (reuse displaySafe semantics minus newline handling) wherever it reaches stderr.\n- **Required regression test:** unit test rejecting `--upload-pack=…`, `-c…`, `ext::…`, and relative-path URLs at plan validation; test asserting ESC bytes injected into a fake CloneRunner's output do not appear in stderr bytes.\n\n## Defended non-issues\n\n1. **`serve --listen` loopback validation** (serve_commands.go:119-139): numeric-only `net.ParseIP` + `IsLoopback`, zone rejection, port bounds, whitespace rejection; validated before workspace discovery (test-pinned order). DNS names, octal/hex literals, and unbracketed IPv6 all fail closed. Non-issue.\n2. **TTY-less confirmation prompts** (defaults_commands.go:125-144, skills_commands.go:148-167, study_commands.go:277-316): EOF/non-\"yes\" deterministically take the conservative branch (keep files / refuse replacement with ExitPartial); destructive automation requires explicit `--force`/`--yes`; reset confirmation precedes durable acceptance so refused resets create no runs. Piped-stdin accidents require stdin content that is literally yes/y. Non-issue under the documented flag-gated automation model.\n3. **`code --output` writes outside the workspace** (code_commands.go:56-66): explicit operator flag, absolute-or-cwd resolution — capability-equivalent to shell redirection on the same machine; contrast `study prompt --output` which is correctly contained via `workspace.ResolveInside`. Not a vulnerability under the stated trust boundary; noting the asymmetry only as intentional-looking design.\n4. **Secret disclosure via renderers:** `config show` renders only `config.Redact(effective)`; health/status/QA/study messages pass `config.RedactValue` at every sink I traced; `smoke.environment` cannot carry values (validated `[A-Z_0-9]` names only, config.go:501-505,577-587); env summary prints counts, not values. Found no secret-bearing sink on stdout/stderr outside F2(b)'s remote-output path.\n5. **`openBrowser` subprocess** (main.go:45-62): exec form (no shell), target derived from the strictly validated listen address, 5 s timeout. Non-issue.\n6. **Durable acceptance coverage:** all ten inventory-pinned runtime-backed call sites accept before runtime work; parse/discover/config failures occur before acceptance so malformed invocations create no rows (verified ordering per arm). Caveat for the spine review: `TestEveryRuntimeBackedCLIEntryUsesDurableAcceptanceInventory` pins call counts and kind strings textually but would not catch a brand-new file adding runtime-backed work with zero `beginDurableCLICommand` calls unless its case row is added.\n7. **QA cancellation→8 vs generic→7 asymmetry and dual envelope families:** both match their in-tree contracts (cli-reference.md:363 documents the QA mapping explicitly; phase3-json-schemas.md fixes schema_version additivity). Contract ambiguity for unnamed envelopes (flow/metrics/storage) is a documentation gap, not a defect with an observable bad outcome beyond consumer confusion already flagged by the context pack.\n\n## Verification notes\n\n- Forward-direction reproduction used only the frozen binary and a scratch workspace; commands and outputs quoted above were captured verbatim during this session.\n- Inverse-direction chain verified line-by-line (no wrapping introduces \"runtime\" between agentwrap and the ladder); realistic rate-limit rendering taken from the pinned agentwrap module source (v0.0.0-20260825130518-dccd575bd101).\n- Git injection primitives tested directly against git 2.55.0 and end-to-end through the binary; negative results reported as negative results.\nRESULT" action.permission=bash action.action=allow action.pattern=*
